courses.title: Deductive Logic - HONORS
courses.description: This course is a study of the concepts and methods of deductive logic, emphasizing formal proof techniques in sentential and predicate logic. Students in this course will be expected to complete additional assignments in order to gain further proficiency in formal logical methods.

courses.title: Ethics - HONORS
courses.description: This course is an integrated and multicultural study of ethical philosophy and emphasizes topics such as the good life, the nature of value, moral reflection, moral reasoning, and action. Many approaches to ethics, including Western and non-Western traditions will be examined. Students in this honors course will be expected to complete extra assignments to gain a deeper insight into moral philosophy.

courses.title: Introduction to Philosophy
courses.description: This is an introduction to the scope and methods of the philosophical discipline, including topics in epistemology (the study of knowledge) and metaphysics (the study of reality), and ethics. Pluralistic approaches will be applied to classical and contemporary problems, issues, and figures.

courses.title: Social and Political Philosophy
courses.description: This course examines fundamental issues and methods in social and political philosophy. Emphasis is placed upon historical development as well as contemporary issues and cultural contexts. Issues covered include political authority, rights, equality, freedom, agency, responsibility, justice, and social identity.

courses.title: History of Western Philosophy - Ancient Greece
courses.description: This course examines the problems of knowledge, reality, truth, value, agency, morality, and wisdom in Greek philosophy from Thales to Aristotle. Emphasis will be given to applications of Greek thinking to social, aesthetic, cultural, gender, historical, and religious issues.

courses.title: History of Western Philosophy - 1400-1800

Students will examine the problems of knowledge, reality, truth, freedom, agency, morality, and value theory in figures from Descartes to Kant, including philosophers from marginalized groups.

courses.title: Critical Thinking and Writing
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the study of argumentation, critical evaluation, the structure of language in written composition, and research techniques. Practical applications of critical thinking skills in everyday situations such as moral thinking, problem-solving, and the evaluation of arguments. Additionally, arguments will be studied within the context of philosophical issues, texts, and subject matter. A major research paper is also required for the course.

courses.title: Asian Philosophy
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the major themes and figures of Asian philosophical traditions, emphasizing those found in China, India, and Japan. Studies may include Confucianism, Mohism, Yangism, Taoism, the Upanishads, Vedanta, Jaina, Buddhism, Zen, and Shinto. Classical thought will be primarily emphasized, though some attention will be given to contemporary thinkers.

courses.title: Philosophy of Religion
courses.description: This course is a systematic introduction to the investigation of religious experience, belief, and life under the scope of philosophy. It covers issues such as philosophical accounts of ultimate reality or God, arguments to justify theistic or atheistic belief, rational accounts of the afterlife and religious experiences, the relationship between faith and reason, the nature of religious language, and how to make sense of evil and suffering in the world.

courses.title: Introduction to Existentialism
courses.description: This course examines central figures, texts, and ideas within existential philosophy, with an emphasis on the fundamental ontological assumption held by all existentialists, namely the existentialists' rejection of rationalism and the idea that a metaphysical system can (or should) describe the world as containing determinate essences that confer univocal conceptual identities upon things, situations, and actions.
